name: Orbis Six Origins
tag: Builds and runs a curated store of goods from six origins, from sourcing to listings to delivery dates.

scenarios.title: Build the launch catalog
scenarios.ask: Build a launch catalog with {per} products from each of our six origins, average price ${=price}, at a {markup} markup.
steps: Sourcing agent
Shortlisted {=per * 6} products from supplier lists for China, Japan, Africa, Canada, Mexico and Thailand, {per} per origin.
Story writer
Wrote a short origin note for each product: where it is made, what it is made of and how to care for it.
Pricing agent
Set prices at a {markup} markup. Average landed cost is about ${=round(price / markup, 2)} per item.
Shipping agent
Grouped products by delivery window so each listing shows an honest arrival estimate.
Reviewer
Flagged {=max(1, round(per * 6 * 0.05))} listings that need better photos before launch.
followups: Do I need to hold inventory?
Not for every item. The store supports supplier-shipped products alongside a small stock of your best sellers, and each listing shows which is which so delivery dates stay accurate.
Why does the margin matter so much?
International shipping, returns and payment fees come out of gross profit. At ${=round(price - price / markup, 2)} per sale you can see quickly whether a product can carry those costs.
Can I keep the catalog balanced across origins?
Yes. The Sourcing agent keeps the same number of products per origin unless you change it, so no region crowds out the others.

scenarios.title: Plan a holiday campaign
scenarios.ask: We expect {visitors} visitors in December. Plan a gift campaign and estimate sales at a {=conv}% conversion rate.
steps: Merch agent
Built six gift guides, one per origin, plus a mixed 'around the world' set.
Copy agent
Wrote email and social copy that leads with the maker stories.
Shipping agent
Set order-by dates per origin so gifts arrive before the holiday.
Forecast
Estimated orders and revenue from your inputs. This is a planning estimate, not a promise.
followups: Which origin should lead the campaign?
The forecast ranks origins by past add-to-cart rates. In this sample, Japan and Mexico lead for gifts under ${=aov}.
What if conversion is only half?
Then you would expect about {=round(visitors * conv / 200)} orders and ${=round(visitors * conv / 200 * aov)}. Plan ad spend against that lower case.

scenarios.title: Check supplier reliability
scenarios.ask: We place about {orders} supplier orders a month and {=late}% arrive late. Which suppliers are the problem?
steps: Tracker
Matched {orders} orders to promised and actual arrival dates.
Analyst
{=max(1, round(orders * late / 100))} late orders. About 70% come from 3 suppliers.
Shipping agent
Two of those suppliers ship by sea without saying so on the quote.
Planner
Suggested backup suppliers for the worst one and longer delivery windows on affected listings.
followups: It drafts the message with the late-order evidence. You review and send it.
Why update listings instead of only switching suppliers?
Customers mind late surprises more than longer honest estimates. Fixing the estimate protects reviews while you test backups.
